extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Coverage & Payment Rationale

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health uses CMS national coverage determinations and applicable mandatory local

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: coverage determinations where possible. Devoted Health also uses InterQual® criteria as a

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: clinical-evidence tool to help guide level-of-care and payment determinations. InterQual® is applied

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: in conjunction with physician review of all relevant clinical information to make medical-necessity

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: determinations.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: All determinations for acute admission coverages are made in accordance with Medicare coverage

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: standards, including the Two-Midnight Benchmark (42 CFR § 412.3) and Devoted Health's obligation

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: under 42 CFR § 422.101(c) to follow original Medicare coverage criteria.1, 2, 3

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Acute Admission Criteria & Documentation Requirements

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Baseline Criteria

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Clinical documentation supporting acute admission payment must demonstrate all of the following4:

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Severity of illness and intensity of services that cannot be safely managed in an outpatient or

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: observation setting.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Predictability of adverse events or risk of clinical deterioration.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Need for diagnostic or therapeutic interventions requiring hospital admission.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Relevant co-morbidities or medical history that increase risk or complexity.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Admitting physician's reasonable expectation that the hospital care will cross at least two

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: midnights, as documented in the medical record, unless documentation supports a

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: case-by-case exception.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health may request additional documentation (e.g., progress notes, imaging reports, labs,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ED records, etc.) when the initial submission is incomplete or ambiguous as to whether the clinical

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: severity meets these requirements.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Concurrent and Retrospective Review

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: All acute admissions are subject to concurrent review against the criteria above. If the review results

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: in the determination that documentation does not support inpatient- or observation-level care,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: payment may be appropriately classified to a lower payment rate.5

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Lower Severity Level of Care

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Lower severity-level services are appropriate for conditions requiring short-term monitoring,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: reassessment, or treatment expected to resolve within a limited timeframe.6

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Examples include (but are not limited to): abdominal pain, allergic reaction, altered mental status,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: anemia, asthma, atrial fibrillation, back pain, bronchitis/bronchiolitis, cellulitis, chest pain, COPD,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: croup, dehydration, diabetes mellitus, epistaxis, febrile illness, gastroenteritis, heart failure,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: hemoptysis, migraine, pneumonia, poisoning/toxic ingestion, renal colic, seizures, syncope/collapse,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: TIA, urinary tract infection, vaginal bleeding (non-obstetrical), and weakness.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: If after 48 hours the patient's condition has not improved sufficiently for discharge, the facility must

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: submit updated clinical documentation supporting conversion to inpatient care.7

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Conversion / Reclassification Requests

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Hospitals may request conversion of a lower-acuity stay payment to higher-acuity inpatient payment

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: when new documentation supports higher-acuity inpatient-level of care.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Requests must be accompanied with additional clinical documentation and reviews will follow a

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: process consistent with Medicare standards and this policy (see Section 3 above).

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Exceptions & Inpatient-Only Procedures

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: This policy does not supersede applicable CMS regulations or contractual terms.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Inpatient payment applies as directed by CMS, including for procedures listed on CMS Addendum E

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: (Inpatient-Only Procedures List), published annually under the Hospital Outpatient Prospective

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Payment System (OPPS) Final Rule in accordance with 42 CFR § 419.22(n), and for other

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: We cover medically necessary services provided at a CAH. Under this policy, the same benefit limits

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: and prior authorization requirements for inpatient and outpatient services apply as those performed

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: in an acute care hospital. Covered services include:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Anesthesia services;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Facilities and related equipment (e.g., operating room);

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Laboratory Services;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Medical social services;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Medications and supplies used during the course of treatment;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: How to bill us

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: We reimburse claims according to Medicare payment rules. CAHs are exempt from PPS rules and are

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: instead paid on a reasonable cost basis calculated by the facility's CCR. For specific details regarding

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: the submission of your FIRLs, please refer to your contact.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Bill your inpatient claims on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) or X12 837I electronic equivalent, with bill type

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: 0111-0119. Be sure to include the appropriate revenue, HCPCS, and ICD-10-PCS codes.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Outpatient claims for CAHs can be submitted using one of the two CMS-approved billing methods, as

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: outlined below. Our billing follows the specific method chosen by the CAH, in line with CMS

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: regulations.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Method I (Standard): Separate Billing for Facility and Professional Charges3

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Facility and professional charges are submitted separately and follow industry coding standards:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Facility services are submitted on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) or an X12 837I transaction;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Use type of bill 085X and the appropriate frequency code (e.g., 0851, 0857).

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Facility claims will be reimbursed at the CCR.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Professional services are submitted on a CMS-1500 or X12 837P transaction;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Use place of service 19 or 22;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Professional claims will be reimbursed at the lesser of billed charges or 100% of the

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: locality-based facility rate of the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Method II (Optional): Combined Billing for Facility and Professional Charges4

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Facility and professional charges are submitted on the same claim and must use the following coding

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: standards:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ All services are submitted on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) or an X12 837I transaction;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Use type of bill 085X and the appropriate frequency code (e.g., 0851, 0857);

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Professional services are billed with the appropriate CPT/HCPCS code and one of the

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: following revenue codes: 096X, 097X, or 098X

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Facility charges will be paid at the CCR; while professional services are paid at 115% of the

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: locality-based facility rate of the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: For CAHs using Method I, this approach remains in place by default unless the CAH proactively opts

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: into Method II with CMS.5 Once a CAH selects Method II, CMS mandates that this choice remain

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: effective for all future cost reporting periods unless a written request to terminate the election is

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: submitted to CMS at least 30 days before the start of the next period.6 Consequently, our billing

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: practices are governed by CMS classifications, and any billing method preference changes must be

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: completed with CMS first.

extracted_content.content: This policy outlines our requirements for National Drug Code (NDC) information to ensure

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: National Drug Code (NDC) information. NDCs serve as standardized identifiers for

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: medications, capturing key details such as the manufacturer, drug name, and dosage. To

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: qualify for reimbursement, claims must include a valid NDC number, the NDC unit of measure,

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: and the total NDC quantity dispensed on all drug claim lines. The policy reinforces adherence

extracted_content.content: Providers are required to include NDC information on all drug claim lines for reimbursement.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Drug claim lines billed without the complete NDC information (valid NDC number, NDC UOM,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: and quantity) may be subject to denial, including denial of all associated lines.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: NDCs are 11-digit numbers that identify the drug manufacturer, name, dosage, strength,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: package size, and quantity. The number is composed of three segments, denoted in a 5-4-2

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: format and can typically be found on the product's label or packaging. For multi-unit

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: packaging, such as a box with several vials, the NDC from the outer packaging should be used.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: If the NDC on the packaging has fewer than 11 digits, leading zeros are required.

extracted_content.content: Examples are outlined below; placeholders have been indicated with an asterisk.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: NDCs should be submitted in the normalized 11-digit format, with no dashes or spaces. Please
